title: The uncle as a pear
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Wood draws the uncle as a pear. Daumier's way. The uncle sees it. He looks at it a long time and says 'more at the bottom.' It's the only art direction he ever gives.

panels.composition: The pad: the UNCLE as a pear — the rain hood the stem, the flat face, the width at the bottom. Cruel and exact.

image.prompt: close on a drawing pad with a caricature of an old man as a pear in a rain hood, cruel and exact, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The uncle, at the shack door, looking at it over WOOD's shoulder. A long time. GULLY frozen at the tank.

image.prompt: an old man in a rain hood looking over a young man's shoulder at a drawing while a teenager freezes at a bait tank, black and white, no words
an old weathered man's face, flat, considering, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Wood adding more at the bottom. The uncle nodding once and going in. Gully breathing. The pear, improved.

image.prompt: a young man widening the bottom of a caricature on a pad while an old man nods once and turns into a shack, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: 'More at the bottom.' The uncle's only art direction, ever.
